title: Phase Gate Decider Playbook
content:
Purpose: quick-reference playbook for deciding phase gates across feature rollouts (canary -> staged -> global). Combines quantitative KPI thresholds, pragmatic checklists, and a lightweight decision tree so product ops and engineering can make consistent go/no-go calls.

Context and scope:
- Intended for mid-to-large product launches where staged rollout and automated routing are used (hosted API + Dedicated).
- Assumes telemetry is available in Console dashboards (per-route latency, token cost per request, error-rate, adoption cohorts).
- Designed to be used during Release Week and the 72h immediate window after each stage change.

How to use this doc:
1) Populate the small KPI tracker below for the feature and the target cohort (canary% bucket, region).
2) Run the preflight checklist before promoting to next stage.
3) Use the decision rules (green/amber/red) to escalte or block.
4) If amber, run mitigations (throttle, smaller cohort, fallback model) and re-evaluate within the defined measurement window.

KPI tracker (fill per-stage):
- Feature: [short name]
- Stage: [Canary / Staged / Global]
- Cohort size: [e.g., 5% USA]
- Measurement window: [e.g., 30m rolling / 2h aggregate]

KPIs and threshold guidance (examples)
- Latency (p50/p95):
  - Green: p95 <= 450ms (hosted), p95 <= 600ms (dedicated heavy sequence)
  - Amber: p95 between 450-700ms
  - Red: p95 > 700ms -> block or rollback to previous model/variant
- Error rate (5xx + model failures):
  - Green: <= 0.1%
  - Amber: 0.1% - 0.5% (investigate, enable degraded-mode routing)
  - Red: > 0.5% -> halt promotion and open incident
- Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics):
  - Green: within planned budget +/- 10%
  - Amber: 10-30% over budget (apply batching suggestions, quantize where safe)
  - Red: >30% over -> stop and investigate quantization/profile
- Quality signal (regression on golden prompts / eval set):
  - Green: 0 - 0.5% regression in correctness metrics
  - Amber: 0.5 - 2% -> manual QA and targeted prompt tuning
  - Red: >2% -> block and revert model or fallback policy
- Adoption and retention leading indicator: new-user conversion from feature >= expected baseline * 0.8 (amber if lower, red if <0.5x)

Preflight checklist (before lifting canary or increasing cohort):
- [ ] Ownership: feature owner, oncall SRE, product-ops lead, and solutions engineer are present for rollout window
- [ ] Instrumentation: route-level tracing, token-level cost logging, and sample request capture enabled
- [ ] Rollback plan: automated traffic-split rollback configured in Console; clear fallback model pinned
- [ ] Alerts: console alarms for p95 latency, error spike, and quality regression are created and tested
- [ ] Canary cohort defined in feature flagging system and validated (labels, regions)
- [ ] Load test sanity: smoke test synthetic traffic at 2x expected canary QPS completed
- [ ] Communication: release slack channel created; stakeholders notified (GTM, CS, legal if required)

Decision matrix (operationalized):
- Measurement window: default 60 minutes after stage change unless metric requires longer (quality evals run for 4h)
- If all KPIs green -> promote next stage after documented signoff
- If any KPI amber -> apply mitigation steps and re-evaluate in 30-60 min (must log mitigations and results)
- If any KPI red -> immediate rollback to previous compatible variant and postmortem triggered

Mitigation playbook (order matters):
1) Throttle cohort size (cut in half) and remeasure for 30min
2) Enable prefix/KV cache warming for common prompts (console cache commands)
3) Switch to compatible lower-latency model variant with feature-parity (automated fallback route)
4) Enable degraded features (disable non-critical tool-calls, reduce max tokens)
5) Contact infra/serving-runtime if kernel/compilation issues suspected

Signoff template (to paste into rollout channel):
- Stage -> [Canary 5% US-WEST]
- Owner -> [name]
- Measurement window -> [60m]
- KPIs observed -> p50: 120ms, p95: 430ms, errors: 0.03%, cost delta: +6%
- Decision -> Promote / Hold / Rollback (circle one)
- Notes -> [short rationale if hold or rollback]

Lightweight tracker table (copy into a sheet for multi-feature coordination):
Columns: feature, stage, cohort_pct, start_time, p95_latency, error_rate, cost_delta_pct, quality_regression_pct, owner, decision, notes
Row example: smart-suggest, canary, 5%, 2024-10-11T10:05Z, 420ms, 0.02%, +4%, 0.1%, Asha Patel, promote, "smoke tests ok"

Escalation ladder:
- Triage: feature owner + oncall SRE + product-ops
- If unresolved after 60m: Eng manager + SRE lead + Infra
- If unresolved after 3h or severity P0: Pager duty -> Exec oncall alert and incident commander assigned

Post-promotion audits (within 72h):
- Verify long-tail latencies p99 and cost run-rate vs projection
- Run weekly quality eval pipeline against holdout prompts for 2 weeks
- Capture any customer support tickets tied to the feature and tag in product-ops tracker

Notes and heuristics from past launches:
- Small logic: quality regressions are often localized to 3-5 prompts; create targeted prompt sets before rollback decision if possible.
- Cost spikes frequently correlate with unbounded max tokens or inadvertent reruns of heavy batch predictions; cap max tokens in rollout window.
- Canary size is not just percent; user type matters (internal beta users vs surface-level public traffic). Prefer low-risk cohorts for early canaries.

Open questions / to do:
- Confirm default measurement window for quality evals across model families (quantized vs fp16) -> action: Maya to draft proposal
- Add an automated slack bot step to populate the tracker row at stage change -> action: Jonah to PR for rollout-tooling

Appendix A: quick shell commands
- Console API to set traffic split: curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/traffic -d '{"feature":"FEATURE","percent":5}' (replace with safe wrapper)
- Revert route: rollout-tooling revert --route FEATURE --to-tag stable-2024-09-xx

Appendix B: quick glossary
- Canaries: limited-cohort test used to validate runtime and quality under production traffic
- Stage: named rollout band (canary -> staged -> global)
- Golden prompts: canonical prompt set used for automated quality checks

End.
